basis.gap: No anchor fact covers this claim. This is a gap in the record, not a weak verdict: there is nothing to check the claim against yet.
basis.notVerifiable: Not a verifiable assertion. This is the kind of statement no document could ever settle: a counterfactual, a prediction, a statement of intent, a legal conclusion, or a claim too vague to check. Set aside rather than scored.

claimDetail.escalatedReview: Escalated to the evidence team; no verdict to confirm or dispute here until the underlying conflict is resolved.
claimDetail.interpretationCaveat: A contributing fact carries a substantive interpretation caveat: what the evidence means, not the medium it came in, is what is uncertain.

notVerifiable.reopenExplanation: Set aside as not verifiable. If this is actually a checkable claim, re-open it: AVT keeps your reclassification and runs only the record-check it skipped.
notVerifiable.reopenedPending: Re-opened as a checkable claim. It shows as No coverage until the document is verified again.

note.placeholder: Record a correction or an explanation. Saving records the note against this claim only; it does not change the verdict or the anchor-fact record.

claimDetail.overrideNotice: Overridden to {verdict}; the analysis below is the tool's own, shown unchanged.
claimDetail.overrideTooltip: A reviewer has recorded a different verdict. The analysis below is the tool's own, unchanged.

recordConflict.description: Two anchor facts speak to the same point ({subject}) but disagree. Both are high-confidence sources, so this is not a reliability problem: the record itself is internally inconsistent. AVT withholds a verdict rather than score the claim, because picking one record over the other is a judgement for you to make and record, not one the tool should make silently.
recordConflict.escalatedNotice: Flagged for the evidence team. The record conflict stays open and counted until a governing record is chosen.
recordConflict.governed: {value} governs: the claim is judged against this record. The other record stays on file.
recordConflict.suggestedNotice: A document's record is suggested over a witness's account. Confirm it, or choose the other record.
recordConflict.title: Conflicting evidence in the record

claimDetail.reopenedTooltip: A reviewer re-classified this as a checkable fact; a live record check is still pending.
claimDetail.verdictByGenerativeModel: Verdict by the generative model; the decision model did not settle it

fact.hint: Objective, checkable assertion, scored against the record. Includes claims framed as admissions or denials: judged on the underlying proposition, not the bare words.

opinion.hint: A value judgement or characterisation: no document can confirm or contradict it, so it is set aside, not scored.
opinion.label: Opinion

unverifiable.hint: An assertion no document could ever settle: a counterfactual, a prediction, a statement of intent or belief, a legal conclusion, or a claim too vague to check. Set aside, not scored. Distinct from No coverage, which is a checkable fact the record is merely silent on.
unverifiable.label: Not verifiable

confidence.tooltip: Interpretive confidence: how unambiguous this evidence's meaning is. Independent of the source medium (handwriting, scan, etc.).

disposition.contested: The verdict is clean, but a contributing fact's interpretation is contested; worth your eyes before sign-off.
disposition.contradicted: The record departs from this claim. A human call is needed before this verdict stands.
disposition.nocover: No fact on the list covers this yet.
disposition.notverifiable: Set aside as not verifiable; sign-off is optional. Re-open below if it's actually checkable.
disposition.recordconflict: Two exhibits in the record disagree. Resolve which governs above, or flag the evidence team; the tool won't pick for you.
disposition.restsOnHeld: A fact this verdict rests on is held for review; confirm the verdict still stands without it, or re-check the claim once the fact is settled.
disposition.scopeMismatch: A cited fact covers a different scope than the claim. Weigh whether it settles the claim as worded before the verdict stands.
disposition.supported: The record affirms this. Your sign-off confirms the tool read it correctly; no judgement call needed.
disposition.tension: The record only partly supports this. Weigh the supporting and conflicting facts above before the verdict stands.
disposition.testimonyOnly: The record affirms this, but no document's record backs it: it rests on testimony. Your sign-off confirms the tool read it correctly; the verdict stays marked as resting on testimony.
disposition.unsourcedOnly: The record affirms this, but only through facts with no source yet. Your sign-off confirms the tool read them correctly; the facts stay marked as unsourced.
